column3: The Hebrew leaves the person whom Gehazi meets unnamed; BSB names Elisha.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed, speaks of going up, and repeats possessive body parts. BSB names Elisha and supplies the bed.
The Hebrew says “house,” specifies once each way, and leaves the subject unnamed; BSB says “room” and names Elisha.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed at both speeches; BSB names Elisha.
The Hebrew says the sons of the prophets sat “before him”; BSB says “at his feet.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB names Elisha.
The Hebrew separately mentions fresh grain in his sack alongside twenty barley loaves; BSB describes a sack of twenty barley loaves made from the first ripe grain.
The Hebrew asks how to set “this” before a hundred men and leaves the second speaker unnamed; BSB specifies twenty loaves and names Elisha.
